items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: When I left around here, come Al Hooks. What are you doing in here? He played several numbers too.

ctx.x: Roll the truck in there. I rolled the piano in there and we rolled on up there. Now the biggest thing was getting the piano out on the ground. We got up there and they had so many waiters. They had so much help up there. And they thought that wasn't a problem. And we got ready to come home. They picked it up and put it back on the truck. Julius, do you want to rent it again? I said, well... I said, I don't know. I said, I'll find out where it's going to be. And they were so glad to get that piano. Well, my piano…

to please. You don't be trying to please yourself. What are some of your favorite numbers? Well, what do you really get a kick out of line? I can't call it. Oh, you mean the, uh, I love Dixieland. Just any of them. I love Dixieland. I love the progressive. In other words, I love practically all numbers, but just like, I can't get this uh, big little number of these guys playing today.
